answer: Persistent workload history. Each identity must carry a continuous thread of solved tasks, verified by random spot-checks against prior outputs. New identities start with zero history, so a clone pays full compute cost to rebuild a credible record before earning anything, while an honest agent reuses its existing record at no extra cost. History is hashed into a public marble ledger; any identity whose task plume diverges from its recorded pattern is dropped. Cloning thus costs more than honest continuation.
